file_count.label: Source files
file_count.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
file_count.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

code_lines.label: Code lines
code_lines.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
code_lines.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

token_count.label: Code tokens
token_count.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
token_count.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

median_file_lines.definition: Median code lines per measured file
median_file_lines.label: Typical file length
median_file_lines.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
median_file_lines.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

largest_file_share.definition: Largest measured file code lines / measured code lines
largest_file_share.label: Code in the largest file
largest_file_share.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
largest_file_share.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

routine_count.label: Functions or programs
routine_count.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
routine_count.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

median_routine_lines.label: Typical function length
median_routine_lines.rationale: Smaller coherent functions can make local reasoning and changes easier.
median_routine_lines.limit: No routines is inapplicable, not zero length. Shorter functions are not invariably better.

max_routine_lines.label: Longest function or program
max_routine_lines.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
max_routine_lines.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

branch_count.label: Control-flow constructs
branch_count.rationale: Project size and organization help interpret differences between deposits.
branch_count.limit: Descriptive context; larger or smaller values are not inherently better.

max_nesting.definition: Maximum control-flow nesting, reset at routine boundaries
max_nesting.label: Maximum nesting depth
max_nesting.rationale: Nested control flow requires readers to keep more conditions in mind.
max_nesting.limit: A maximum grows with project size; complexity may be required by the task.

top_level_share.label: Code outside functions
top_level_share.rationale: Encapsulation can make responsibilities and dependencies easier to isolate.
top_level_share.limit: Linear analysis scripts can be appropriate. This is structural context, not a penalty.

line_over_100.definition: line over 100 findings per 1,000 measured code lines
line_over_100.label: Long code lines
line_over_100.rationale: Very long lines can make code harder to scan.
line_over_100.limit: A formatting convention, not demonstrated comprehension or correctness; R uses native lintr instead.

working_directory_change.definition: working directory change findings per 1,000 measured code lines
working_directory_change.label: Working-directory changes
working_directory_change.rationale: Directory changes describe execution context that readers may need to reconstruct.
working_directory_change.limit: Lexical spelling matches do not establish a filesystem failure or resolve function identities.

dependency_declaration.definition: Presence of observed dependency declaration evidence
dependency_declaration.label: Direct dependencies declared
dependency_declaration.rationale: Explicit requirements help others identify the packages the analysis needs.
dependency_declaration.limit: Lockfiles record a resolved environment, not direct requirements. Unobserved does not mean absent from all documentation.

version_constraint.definition: Presence of observed version constraint evidence
version_constraint.label: Dependency version constraints recorded
version_constraint.rationale: Recorded software requirements and versions can help reconstruct an environment.
version_constraint.limit: Supported Softverse inventory evidence only, including bundled packages; absence is not verified lack of documentation, and presence does not establish restoration.

locked_dependency.definition: Presence of observed locked dependency evidence
locked_dependency.label: Locked dependencies recorded
locked_dependency.rationale: Recorded package versions can reduce changes caused by different software environments.
locked_dependency.limit: Does not establish complete environment coverage, successful restoration, or that this environment produced the results.

bundled_dependency.definition: Presence of observed bundled dependency evidence
bundled_dependency.label: Bundled dependency evidence
bundled_dependency.rationale: Recorded software requirements and versions can help reconstruct an environment.
bundled_dependency.limit: Supported Softverse inventory evidence only, including bundled packages; absence is not verified lack of documentation, and presence does not establish restoration.

interpreter_version.definition: Presence of observed interpreter version evidence
interpreter_version.label: version recorded
interpreter_version.rationale: Interpreter versions help explain and potentially reproduce version-dependent behavior.
interpreter_version.limit: A recorded version is not evidence that all deposited scripts used it; free-text documentation is not covered.

indentation_linter.label: Indentation findings
indentation_linter.rationale: Consistent indentation helps readers see code structure.
indentation_linter.definition: Selected lintr indentation findings per 1,000 measured nonblank, noncomment code lines; both measurements must be complete.
indentation_linter.limit: Conformance to lintr's convention, not a direct measure of comprehension; inline suppressions are honored.

line_length_linter.label: Long-line findings
line_length_linter.rationale: Very long lines can make code harder to scan.
line_length_linter.definition: Selected lintr findings for lines over 100 characters per 1,000 measured code lines; both measurements must be complete.
line_length_linter.limit: The 100-character threshold is a convention. Findings can concern comments and strings as well as code.

duplicate_argument_linter.label: Duplicate-argument candidates
duplicate_argument_linter.rationale: Repeated argument names can indicate an unintended call or cause an evaluation error.
duplicate_argument_linter.definition: At least one duplicate_argument_linter finding in a completely linted deposit.
duplicate_argument_linter.limit: Candidates require source context; presence does not establish an incorrect research result.

equals_na_linter.label: NA-comparison candidates
equals_na_linter.rationale: Equality comparisons with NA can fail to implement the intended missing-value check.
equals_na_linter.definition: At least one equals_na_linter finding in a completely linted deposit.
equals_na_linter.limit: This is one narrow error pattern; no findings does not imply reliable code.

stopifnot_present.label: Explicit stopifnot checks
stopifnot_present.rationale: Explicit assertions can detect violated assumptions before errors propagate.
stopifnot_present.definition: At least one flowR-recognized base stopifnot call in a deposit with complete flowR processing.
stopifnot_present.limit: Other assertion and testing APIs are not covered. Presence does not show execution or adequate checking.

absolute-file-paths.label: Absolute filesystem paths
absolute-file-paths.rationale: Machine-specific paths can require edits before another researcher can run the code.
absolute-file-paths.definition: At least one flowR absolute-file-paths finding in a deposit with complete flowR processing.
absolute-file-paths.limit: Some absolute paths are deliberate and portable within a specified environment; unresolved paths remain undetected.

random_without_seed_call.label: Randomness with no supplied seed
random_without_seed_call.rationale: Uncontrolled random initialization can make repeated computations differ.
random_without_seed_call.definition: Among completely processed deposits with recognized stochastic calls: no recognized seed-setting call with a supplied non-NULL seed expression anywhere in the measured R code.
random_without_seed_call.limit: The API catalog is incomplete. A seed call can use a changing value or be unrelated to the random operation; RNG-state restoration and cross-file execution order are not resolved.
